title: WalkMe alternatives in 2026, without the six-month rollout
summary: Frigade guides people in your SaaS product, Salesforce, Workday, and internal systems. Compare generated guidance with authored flows, including pricing, automation, and employee training.
body_markdown:
Frigade Assistant is a[WalkMe](https://frigade.com/compare/walkme) alternative for guiding people through both your own SaaS product and applications such as Salesforce, Workday, and internal systems. It learns each application by using it, then answers questions and generates walkthroughs for the task someone is trying to finish.


We make Frigade, so that's the approach we favor. The choice is whether you want an assistant to generate guidance from product knowledge or want your team to author the flows. A company-wide training program may also need reporting and publishing controls alongside that guidance.


## The three jobs WalkMe takes on, and the modern alternative for each


For a SaaS app you own, Frigade can answer customer questions and walk people through setup. Appcues, Userpilot, and Pendo also provide in-app onboarding tools. Frigade Engage is our option when you want to build those experiences in React.


For third-party apps, Frigade learns the software your employees use and helps them work in it. Whatfix supports guidance in employee applications, and Pendo offers guides through its browser extension.


For an employee training rollout, Frigade can teach people tasks inside those applications. If the program also requires formal completion records or reports across departments, those requirements belong in the comparison too.

## If you need tours on your own SaaS app


Frigade Assistant learns how your product works and uses that knowledge to generate a walkthrough when someone needs help. A customer can ask how to invite a teammate or change a setting, and get guidance from the screen they're on. You can also offer help through[Suggestions](https://frigade.com/features/suggestions) , such as a prompt to connect an integration after an upgrade.


The work for your team is teaching the agent the product and reviewing its guidance. Frigade[re-learns on scheduled passes](https://frigade.com/features/always-accurate) , and you can request another pass after a release.


Authored flows are useful when you want to control the exact wording and order of an experience. A feature announcement or a standard welcome tour can benefit from that control.[Appcues lets you build those flows on top of your product](https://docs.appcues.com/getting-started/what-is-appcues) ; Frigade Engage gives you React components for the same kind of deliberate authoring.


## If you need tours on a third-party app you don't own


Frigade works in Salesforce, Workday, and internal systems. The agent learns each application the same way it learns a SaaS product you built: by using it. Employees can ask questions and get guidance inside the application they're working in.


That makes Frigade relevant when the problem is teaching people how to use software you didn't build. For example, a new sales hire might ask how to update an opportunity in Salesforce. The assistant can generate a walkthrough for that task instead of requiring your team to prepare a tour for it first.


Whatfix is also an option for this use case: its[plans cover employee applications and multi-app guidance](https://whatfix.com/pricing/) . Pendo supports[extension applications](https://support.pendo.io/hc/en-us/articles/21165049812635-Add-extension-apps) for delivering guides on third-party websites.


## If you need an employee training rollout


Frigade can provide the in-app training for employees using your own software or third-party applications. Someone learning an internal purchasing system can ask how to submit a request and get a walkthrough while doing it.


A formal training program can involve additional work, such as assigning courses, recording completion, and reporting progress to a department lead. Frigade's generated guidance addresses the task inside the application. If you need those administrative functions too, compare them explicitly rather than treating a walkthrough as the whole training program.


[WalkMe's plans](https://www.walkme.com/pricing/) include adoption analytics and administration controls. Whatfix provides guidance analytics and reporting across applications. For onboarding inside a SaaS app, Appcues, Userpilot, and Userflow are also worth considering when you want to author the experience.


## How to pick


Choose Frigade when you want people to ask questions and get guidance without your team writing every walkthrough. That applies to customers in your product and employees in Salesforce, Workday, or internal tools.


Choose an authored flow when the exact sequence is the point, such as an introduction everyone should see. A product can combine a planned welcome experience with an assistant that helps with the questions and tasks that come after it.


## Why "AI" inside WalkMe isn't the same as an AI-native alternative


The useful distinction is how a walkthrough gets made. Frigade's agent[learns the application firsthand](https://frigade.com/how-it-works) and generates guidance from that knowledge. Your team doesn't need to define the steps of each tour.[Enabled Skills](https://frigade.com/features/skills) also let the assistant complete supported tasks from the conversation.


WalkMe and Whatfix have automation too.[ActionBot](https://support.walkme.com/knowledge-base/desktop-menu-actionbot/) runs configured processes, and Whatfix supports[automated steps within Flows](https://support.whatfix.com/docs/flow-automation) . Whatfix also offers[automated testing](https://support.whatfix.com/docs/testing-whatfix-content) and[element reselection automation in beta](https://support.whatfix.com/docs/element-reselection-automation) .


Being able to run a prepared workflow and being able to generate a walkthrough for a new question are different capabilities. When you compare products, ask for help with a task you haven't prepared a tour for. You can see how much of the answer comes from the system's understanding of the application.


The[ProductOnboarding.com report on digital adoption platforms](https://productonboarding.com/articles/state-of-digital-adoption-platforms-2026) discusses these approaches in more detail.


## FAQ


### What is the closest WalkMe alternative for SaaS apps you own?


Frigade Assistant generates guidance from what it learns by using your product. Appcues, Userpilot, and Pendo offer in-app onboarding tools when you want to build the flows yourself. Frigade Engage is our option for authored experiences in React.


### What is the closest WalkMe alternative for overlaying third-party apps like Salesforce or Workday?


Frigade Assistant works in Salesforce, Workday, and internal systems as well as your own SaaS product. It learns each application and guides people through their tasks. Whatfix is another option for employee applications, and Pendo supports guides through its Launcher extension.


### How long does a WalkMe rollout take, and how do alternatives compare?


Rollout time depends on the applications and workflows you need to support. With Frigade, the agent learns the application and generates guidance, so your team does not have to author each tour. Installation and review still need to happen; we do not promise a fixed rollout time for every application.


### Can Frigade replace WalkMe entirely?


Frigade can replace WalkMe for in-app answers and guidance in your SaaS product, third-party applications, and internal systems. If you also use WalkMe for training records, publishing controls, or cross-application reporting, compare those requirements separately. They are distinct from helping someone complete a task in an application.
